what_happened: mcp.py's token resolution is one shared module-level statement executed identically regardless of CLI flag, so all four named code paths (stdio server, --briefing-text, --receipt, --effect-line) were confirmed to fall back to config.json with a single read instead of four separate traces; setup-sapience-mcp.sh's existing whole-entry replacement in process_write() also means the token-removal fix needs no separate migration logic -- the next SessionStart write self-migrates any existing token-bearing entry.

Sibling task 683 (planning, same cycle) declares a file_scope IDENTICAL to this task's five-file territory (setup-sapience-mcp.sh, verify-sapience-mcp.sh, test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh, hooks/sapience-mcp-register-project.sh, per-repo-scoping.md). 682's file_scope was null at plan time and is harvested from this plan, so the overlap only becomes visible to the admission gate after this dispatch's postflight. Phase-level re-read instructions were written into every editing phase and the overlap is named in the plan's Risks table.

The research report's key claims were all re-confirmable cheaply against live state (6 of 6 project entries carry the token; mcp.py's single module-level TOKEN line; config.json 0600), so the plan rests on measured rather than carried figures. Running suite_selection_select once per phase file set yielded honest Tier Justification lines with no guessing, including a correctly-handled mixed-output case for the doc phase.

Discovered during planning (not in the research report): the writer the SessionStart hook actually invokes is $HOME/.claude/scripts/setup-sapience-mcp.sh, a user-level copy placed by install-sapience-mcp-session-hook.sh whose WRITER_SRC is $SCRIPT_DIR/setup-sapience-mcp.sh. A source-store edit therefore does NOT reach production via deploy-headless.sh; the installer must be re-run from the source store. Phase 5 was written around this.

Phase 1's five mcp.py token-resolution probes (statusline, briefing-text, receipt, effect-line, bare stdio initialize) all passed on the first attempt under a stripped environment, confirming unconditionally that no invocation shape requires SAPIENCE_TOKEN -- the plan's contingency branch for a divergent shape never triggered.

verify-touched.sh's Batch Gate Deferral run reported 1 failing suite, test-stall-reprompt-wiring.sh, entirely unrelated to this phase's territory (agent-system/extensions/sapience/**). Root cause: the shared working tree carries unrelated uncommitted changes from concurrently-running sibling sessions (task 677's orchestration work), and verify-touched.sh's whole-tree diff detection picked those up alongside this phase's one touched file. This phase's own scoped suite (test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh) passed 58/0.

Proved case 54's positive assertion is discriminative, not vacuous: reverted setup-sapience-mcp.sh to its pre-Phase-2 (1ad3905a9^) content, re-ran the suite, and confirmed case 54 FAILS (sentinel leaked into the written entry) while 55a/55b still pass. Restored the fix and confirmed 58/0 green again, with git status --short showing the restored file byte-identical (no diff).

Phase 1's record (records/01_mcp-token-resolution-measurement.md) recorded config.json's .token SHA-256[:12] fingerprint as 1ccd05e02475 (len 16). Independently recomputing the same field in Phase 4 (same file, mtime unchanged since before Phase 1 ran) yields fp 20a5377da89a (len 16) -- a different hash at the same length. The file was not modified between the two measurements, so Phase 1's recorded fingerprint value itself appears to have been mistranscribed; this does not affect Phase 1's PASS verdicts, which test resolution behavior (authenticated replies with SAPIENCE_TOKEN stripped) rather than the hash value itself, so build item (2)'s unconditional conclusion stands.

Phase 4's required by-value (not by-filename) comparison across the four candidate token locations surfaced a real, previously undocumented divergence: the token currently resolved by mcp.py (~/.sapience/config.json's .token, 16 chars) matches ~/.config/sf1-hub-ben/env's SAPIENCE_TOKEN and ~/.config/sf1-hub-ben/sapience-token byte-for-byte, but does NOT match /run/secrets/sapience_token (the sops-nix provisioned secret, 43 chars) nor the oldest config.json backup (config.json.bak-20261103-175726, which does match the sops secret). This means the active application token and the sops-managed secret have diverged (likely a manual token rotation in config.json that was never mirrored back into secrets.yaml), corrected in per-repo-scoping.md's new subsection rather than assumed to be in sync as the plan's framing implied.
